summary: Brunei waives visas in tiers — 90 days for US, Canadian, UK, EU and EFTA passports, 30 days for nationalities including Japan, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea and the UAE, and 14 days for nationalities including Cambodia, China, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam — while nationals of Australia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia obtain a visa on arrival and the nationalities in the Foreign Ministry's other categories apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Brunei.

source.name: UK FCDO — Brunei travel advice, entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for travelers aged 9 months or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for those who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in such a country.

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (International Travel and Health)

travelInsurance.text: Canada's travel advice says that when entering Brunei you must be able to show customs officials proof of medical insurance covering your whole stay, and that without it your visa will only be valid for two weeks. No Brunei government source we could read states this rule.

source.name: Government of Canada — Brunei travel advice

onwardTicket.text: Visa applicants must include a copy of a confirmed return flight ticket and proof of accommodation, according to Brunei's foreign ministry. No official source states an onward-ticket check for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Brunei Darussalam — visa information, Category A (required documentation)

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for visitors to Brunei.

declarations.name: Brunei E-Arrival Card
declarations.submitWindow: Before arrival; it can also be done at the immigration control post on your phone
declarations.text: All foreign nationals arriving in or leaving Brunei through a sea, air or land immigration control post must register on the E-Arrival Card portal before arriving, one registration per traveller; it replaced the paper arrival card (Form 19) and is free. Travellers in transit who do not pass through immigration do not need one. Registration needs an account on the Immigration Department's portal, your passport, your address in Brunei and your flight or vehicle details. If you forget, you can register at the immigration control post on your phone.

source.name: Brunei Immigration and National Registration Department — INRS portal, E-Arrival Card FAQ (shown before login)

currencyLimits.text: The US Department of State gives BND 15,000 (about US$11,000) as Brunei's currency limit, both on entry and on exit. No Brunei government source we could read states the threshold.

source.name: US Department of State — Brunei international travel information

notes: The UK says the sale of alcohol and tobacco is illegal in Brunei. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount of alcohol, which must be declared to customs on arrival and drunk in private.

The UK says drug offences can carry the death penalty in Brunei. Canada lists possessing pornographic material, firearms or weapons, gambling, and promoting any religion other than Islam among activities that are illegal and severely punished.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says crime levels are low, with occasional petty crime against tourists and house burglaries, and Canada says violent crime is rare. Canada says Brunei's Sharia penal code applies regardless of a person's religion or nationality.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Brunei travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice gives Brunei's rainy (monsoon) seasons as September to January and May to July. The CIA World Factbook describes the climate as tropical: hot, humid and rainy.

tips.text: The UK says the sale of alcohol is illegal in Brunei. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount for private consumption, and it must be declared to customs on arrival.

The UK says Brunei's penalties for drug offences are severe and in some cases include the death penalty; Canada says death is the mandatory penalty for many narcotics offences, including trafficking even very small amounts.
The UK says that during Ramadan it is against the law to be seen eating or drinking in public during fasting hours, and that you must not smoke in public.
The UK advises dressing modestly in Brunei, for example not wearing shorts in government and public buildings such as health centres.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Many visitors do not. US, Canadian, UK and EU passport holders get 90 days visa-free; nationalities including Japan, Malaysia, Singapore and South Korea get 30 days; and nationalities including Cambodia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam get 14 days. Nationals of Australia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Saudi Arabia obtain a visa on arrival, and the nationalities Brunei's Foreign Ministry lists in its categories A and B apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission — no official Brunei source describes an online e-Visa.

faq.question: Do Australians need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Australians obtain a visa on arrival. Brunei's Foreign Ministry lists the visa on arrival as single or multiple entry, with a visa duration of 30 days and fees of BND 20 or BND 30.

faq.question: Can I drink alcohol in Brunei?
faq.answer: Alcohol cannot be bought in Brunei: the UK says its sale is illegal. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount, which must be declared to customs on arrival and drunk in private.

faq.question: What is the Brunei E-Arrival Card?
faq.answer: A digital arrival declaration. The UK government says foreign visitors must submit it before travelling to Brunei, that it may be requested at check-in, and that you do not need one if you are not passing through immigration. The card is issued through the Immigration Department's portal after you register.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Brunei?
faq.answer: US passport holders can enter visa-free for up to 90 days.
